chunks: Nushuz may occur from both the man and the woman together. As for that which is from the man, it is what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has said in His Book.
And if a woman fears nushuz or aversion from her husband, then there is no blame upon them that they reconcile between themselves by a settlement, and reconciliation is better.

It means that a woman may be with a man and he is not pleased with her, so he wishes to divorce her. Then she says to him: Keep me and do not divorce me, and I leave to you what is upon your responsibility, and I make lawful for you my day and my night. Then that becomes agreeable to him.
Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated that from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

So when the woman commits nushuz like the nushuz of the man, then it is khulʿ. When it is from the woman, it means that she does not obey him in his bed. And this is what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has said.

And those whose nushuz you fear, admonish them, and forsake them in the beds, and strike them. Forsaking means that he turns his back toward her, and striking is with the siwak or something else, a gentle striking.
Then if they obey you, do not seek any way against them. Indeed Allah is Ever Most High, Most Great.

key_terms.اَلنُّشُوزُ: marital rebellion, aversion, or discord between spouses
key_terms.بِالسِّوَاكِ: with the siwak, indicating a light implement
key_terms.خُلْعٌ: a form of separation initiated through the wife’s release from the marriage
key_terms.صُلْحاً: a mutual reconciliation or settlement between spouses

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about nushuz between husband and wife in Islam?
ai.summary: This passage explains that nushuz can come from either spouse and comments on the relevant Quranic verses for each case. It outlines marital reconciliation when aversion comes from the husband, and the legal and practical treatment of nushuz when it comes from the wife, framing both within Quranic guidance.
